mūnis , e, adj. cf. munus,
I.ready to be of service or to oblige, obliging (ante-class.): “dico ejus pro meritis gratum me et munem fore,” Plaut. Merc. prol. 105 : munifici munesque viri, Lucil. ap. Non. 23, 15; cf.: munem significare ... officiosum: unde e contrario immunis dicitur, qui nullo fungitur officio, Paul. ex Fest. p. 143 Müll.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
